A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same HARP work, with accessible text, equations, figures and tables. Appendices A–D are retained; v2 adds Appendices E–F. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection results on four QA datasets, ablations, cross-dataset evaluations and appendix intervention experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds reasoning-patch examples, F1 threshold curves, dataset-composition counts and measured SVD resource consumption.

M1.justification: The HARP detector remains unchanged. Appendix E adds a separate Reasoning Patch intervention that preserves normal semantic components while substituting CoT-derived reasoning components across decoder layers. This extends the intervention procedures beyond v1's component-removal demonstration without replacing the detection algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds mathematical word-problem reasoning using GSM8K examples under normal, few-shot CoT, zero-shot CoT and patched generation. This is a limited task expansion beyond the retained factual QA evaluations and fictitious-city demonstration; no aggregate GSM8K detection benchmark is reported.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Perplexity, LN-Entropy, Semantic Entropy, Lexical Similarity, EigenScore and HaloScope. The new supplementary comparison in Figures 10–11 evaluates normal prompting and few-shot or zero-shot CoT alongside Reasoning Patch, adding comparator conditions for that intervention.

E3.justification: v2 adds F1 evaluation to the threshold sweep, a three-condition reasoning-patch protocol, and SVD time/memory profiling that includes Qwen2.5-72B and Qwen3-235B MoE. The original data split, ten-answer generation setting, correctness thresholds and detector-training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E introduces a substantive mechanism test: whether transferring reasoning-subspace components induces step-by-step reasoning without CoT text. Appendix F adds computational-cost and larger-model spectral analyses, while Figure 6 adds F1 sensitivity. Earlier projection ablations, layer analyses, cross-dataset tests and the Epsilon demonstration are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The median and interquartile-range reporting in Figure 5a is unchanged. The new results introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The main AUROC table, projection-ablation scores and cross-dataset results are unchanged. Substantial supplementary results are added: known/unknown counts, F1 curves, corrected outputs in patch examples, larger-model spectra and SVD measurements. Examples include 293 known versus 3317 unknown NQ-open questions and 9.83 seconds for Qwen2.5-72B SVD. These are new results, not improved main-benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds mathematical time and space complexity expressions for full and truncated SVD, and Appendix E formally defines the patched hidden state. The original direct-sum formulation, low-rank approximation derivation and appendix PCA mathematics remain unchanged; no new proof establishes the semantic meaning of the subspaces.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same claims about subspace decomposition, SVD-based feature construction, dimensionality reduction and detection performance. The added conclusion sentence points to Reasoning Patch as supporting evidence for the existing reasoning-subspace claim rather than redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds explicit causal interpretations: reasoning-component transfer is described as sufficient to induce coherent reasoning, including when the donor CoT contains an error. Appendix F infers larger-model applicability from similar singular-value decay. These substantially extend the mechanism and applicability discussion, although the patch evidence consists of illustrative cases.

D1.justification: Table 2 newly discloses known/unknown question counts. Appendix E supplies CoT prompts and patching instructions, while Appendix F identifies an H100 80GB GPU, matrix dimensions and resource measurements. Appendix A's existing implementation settings are unchanged; these disclosures do not establish changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for chain-of-thought prompting, GSM8K and Qwen3. The related-work positioning otherwise remains stable; replacing author-based mentions with HaloScope and EigenScore does not introduce different cited methods.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved. Changes comprise localized wording, updated cross-references, short links to the new validation experiment, an expanded conclusion and appended Sections E–F. There is no extensive rewriting of the existing exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2, 5 and 6, Figures 9–12, and an F1 panel in Figure 6. The previous Figure 6b cross-dataset heatmap becomes standalone Figure 7 with unchanged values. The new experimental diagram, generation comparisons and resource displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through dataset counts, F1 curves, explicit patch prompts and measured SVD costs, while retaining the original detection evidence. The patch examples provide useful additional mechanism evidence, but only two cases are shown, limiting the broad causal interpretation. Appendix F also conflates matrix storage with full SVD-factor storage in its complexity statement. The net gain is useful but limited.
